sections.h2: Which Lebanon offices share the building at 223 North Spalding Avenue?
sections.html:
The sheriff, the PVA and the County Clerk all list 223 North Spalding Avenue in Lebanon as their address, so a Marion County owner can settle most property tax business in a single visit. Each keeps its own suite.

  • Sheriff's Office, Suite 101 (270-692-3051): bills and payments, open Monday to Friday between 8:30 and 4:30.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, Suite 202 (270-692-3401): value, name and address changes, and exemption applications, with the same Monday to Friday hours.
  • County Clerk, Suite 102 (270-692-2651): deed recording and delinquent bills. The clerk's own site lists 8:20 to 4:20 on weekdays and a Saturday morning session.

The sheriff's FAQ hands off questions about taxable value and bill calculation to the PVA, and questions about delinquent bills or buying a lien to the clerk.

sections.h2: What sets Marion County apart from other central Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Marion County is lightly settled: about 57 people per square mile on 343 square miles of land. The legislature carved it from Washington County in 1834 and named it for Francis Marion. Washington, Boyle, Casey, Taylor, LaRue and Nelson counties surround it.

Lebanon is the seat and the largest of three cities, the others being Loretto and Bradfordsville. Gravel Switch, Nerinx, Raywick and St. Mary are smaller places. Wikipedia notes that planar maps put the state's geographic center about three miles north-northwest of Lebanon near KY 429, though neighboring counties dispute it.

Population has hovered near the same level for a century. The first census after formation, in 1840, counted 11,032 residents; later counts ran 16,887 in 1960 and 17,910 in 1980. The tally was 15,499 in 1930, 16,499 in 1990, 18,212 in 2000, 19,820 in 2010 and 19,581 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate of 20,115 is up 2.8 percent from the 2020 base.

One school district, Marion County Schools, serves every address, with Marion County High School as its comprehensive high school. The Marion County Public Library is in Lebanon. For a farm sale, remember that cropland and pasture are valued by agricultural use under Section 172A of the state constitution, and outbuildings by replacement cost less depreciation.

sections.h2: How do households in Marion County look in the Census data?
sections.html:
Marion County's 2020 to 2024 figures show a settled, owner-heavy community where nearly nine in ten residents stayed in the same house for a year.

Owners with no mortgage carry a median monthly cost of only $415. Median household income is $59,627, and 16.4 percent of residents are in poverty. Among adults 25 and older, 87.2 percent finished high school and 15.1 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Workers commute 22.4 minutes on average, and 1,026 residents are veterans. Employers numbered 353 establishments in 2023 with a combined payroll of $380.7 million.

The local economy leans on services. Health care and social assistance receipts reached $110.1 million in 2022, against $25.7 million for lodging and food service and $22.0 million for transportation and warehousing. Total retail sales were $230.8 million, or $11,689 per resident. Another 1,354 businesses have no employees. Some 22.3 percent of residents are under 18, 15.3 percent of those under 65 report a disability, and 86.3 percent of households have broadband. Density has barely moved, from 57.8 people per square mile in 2010 to 57.1 in 2020. The labor force includes 57.3 percent of residents 16 and older, and 8.7 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance.

sections.h2: What is the sheriff's collection calendar in Marion County?
sections.html:
The sheriff's FAQ says bills go out ahead of October 1. Owners with no bill in hand by October 10 should phone so a copy can be sent.

  • October 1 through November 1: two percent discount.
  • November 2 through December 31: bill at face value.
  • January 1 through 31: a five percent penalty.
  • February 1 through April 15: a twenty-one percent penalty.

The unpaid balance moves to the County Clerk on April 16. The twenty-one percent adds the ten percent penalty of KRS 134.015 to the sheriff's collection add-on.

Mail payments need the bill number on the check, and a stamped, self-addressed envelope brings back a receipt. Card payments are accepted only at the counter, with the card company's fee passed to the payer. The system will not track a partial payment, so send the whole amount at once.

sections.h2: What happens to the bill when a Marion County house sells?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner stays on the bill all year. If the house sells afterward, the sheriff expects the bill to be forwarded in care of the buyer, and a buyer who never gets one can ask the sheriff to mail a copy. The office adds that it carries no responsibility when a bill is missed during a closing.

Mortgage servicers are not sent a copy. Every bill is mailed to the homeowner, who has to pass it along to the lender in time.

For earlier years, call the clerk at 270-692-2651. Overdue bills are transferred there, and the clerk's site advertises a free Online Deed Room. KRS 134.420 lets a tax lien last up to eleven years against the property itself, so a title company will insist that it be paid from the seller's proceeds.

sections.h2: How does a Marion County owner argue with the PVA's number?
sections.html:
Phone 270-692-3401 and request a sit-down. State law makes that meeting the first rung of any appeal, and KRS 133.120 then sends an unresolved case to the clerk as a written petition and on to a hearing. Under KRS 133.030 that hearing opens 25 to 35 days after the inspection period ends.

The Department of Revenue says each Marion County parcel is walked by PVA staff at least once every four years, so ask when your house was last seen. Appraisals and nearby sales carry weight. Payment stays due on the amount you claim.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption do for a Marion County tax bill?
sections.html: It removes $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Applied to the county's median home value of $168,100, the taxable base becomes $119,000. The PVA takes applications from owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who live in the house. Since 19.5 percent of Marion County residents are 65 or older, the exemption reaches a sizable share of owners. It stays with the owner, so a buyer applies separately.

sections.h2: What happens at the Marion County Clerk's counter when I record a deed?
sections.html: The clerk first collects the grantor's transfer tax, which KRS 142.050 sets at fifty cents for every $500 of value or part of $500. A $168,100 sale produces a charge of $168.50. Taxes paid at the clerk's counter can use cash, check, debit or credit card, and the clerk's site warns that cards carry extra fees. Foreclosure sales, divorce transfers between spouses and parent-to-child deeds for nominal value are exempt.

faqs.q: Where is the Marion County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 223 North Spalding Avenue, Suite 101, in Lebanon, phone 270-692-3051. Mailed payments should show the bill number.

faqs.q: How much extra does a Marion County bill cost in February?
faqs.a: The sheriff lists a 21 percent penalty from February 1 to April 15, after 5 percent in January. Bills still open on April 16 go to the clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Marion County sheriff accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff's FAQ says its system does not track partial payments, so send the full bill in one payment.

faqs.q: Which office handles Marion County exemptions?
faqs.a: The PVA, at 270-692-3401. The sheriff refers homestead and disability questions there.

faqs.q: Where do I look up a Marion County delinquent bill?
faqs.a: Call the County Clerk at 270-692-2651. Delinquent bills are transferred to that office, and the clerk's site runs a free Online Deed Room.
